# Temple Scroll Column 42 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)
**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** 11QT (Cave 11), Col. 42 | **Condition:** well preserved

---

**42:1** A clean person must sprinkle the unclean person on the third day and the seventh day, completing the purification on the seventh day.

**42:2** The person who does the sprinkling must wash his clothes afterward. Anyone who touches the purification water becomes unclean until evening.

**42:3** Whatever an unclean person touches becomes unclean, and whoever touches that object becomes unclean until evening.

**42:4** Whenever an unclean person enters a house, everything inside becomes unclean for seven days.

**42:5** Any uncovered container without a tight lid becomes unclean as well.

**42:6** On the seventh day the person is purified; he must wash his clothes, bathe in water, and by evening he will be clean.

**42:7** Anyone who touches a human bone, a slain person, a dead body, or a grave out in the open becomes unclean for seven days.

**42:8** The full purification procedure must be carried out for him: sprinkling on the third day and the seventh day.

**42:9** On the seventh day he becomes clean. He must wash his clothes, bathe, and by sunset he will be clean.

**42:10** If an unclean person out in the open refuses purification, his uncleanness stays on him — and anyone who touches him becomes unclean too.

**42:11** Anyone who touches an unclean person becomes unclean until evening. The one who sprinkles the purification water must wash his clothes.

**42:12** Whoever touches the purification water is unclean until evening, and anything an unclean person touches becomes unclean.

**42:13** The person who touches the contaminated object must wash his clothes, bathe, and will remain unclean until evening.

**42:14** The people of Israel must keep all these rules so they do not defile their camps, where I dwell among them.

**42:15** For I, the LORD, live among the people of Israel. You must set apart your camps and keep them holy.

**42:16** Do not make your camps repulsive with anything unclean, for I am the LORD who lives among you.

---

*PNEUMA notes: This column details how corpse impurity spreads through contact — a kind of ritual chain reaction. The closing verses (14-16) provide the theological reason behind all these purity laws: God himself dwells in the midst of the camp. Contamination is not merely a hygiene concern but a threat to divine presence.*
